title: Data Journalist Roadmap
summary: Build a career combining journalism, data analysis, verification and visual storytelling to investigate public issues, explain complex datasets and produce evidence-based news reports.

facts.Current degree: BJMC / B.A. Journalism & Mass Communication – Data Journalism / Fact-Checking
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a three-year bachelor's degree with an optional fourth-year honours route, subject to your university's regulations. The long-term horizon extends from 2026 to 2046.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: A portfolio of data-backed stories, verified claims, charts and published reporting.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Expertise in areas such as public finance, elections, health reporting, climate, business or investigative journalism.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Senior data journalism, investigative team leadership, newsroom data editing or research management.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Leadership in evidence-based journalism, responsible AI-assisted reporting and independent investigative projects.

blocks.text: Prioritise reporting and verification alongside technical skills. A strong data journalist can explain where data came from, what it measures, what it leaves out and why the findings matter.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If your institution offers a four-year honours programme, use the additional year for a research-intensive investigation, a data-journalism dissertation or an advanced project using reproducible analysis. Verify the programme's current structure and eligibility with your university.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Develop from reporting individual datasets to leading investigations, reviewing analytical methods and mentoring journalists. Learn computational methods and AI-assisted research, but verify outputs against primary sources. Protect confidential sources, disclose uncertainty and never confuse correlation with causation.

blocks.label: Eligibility note
blocks.text: Read the specific notice for degree, year, age, citizenship and portfolio conditions. The Prime Minister's Internship Scheme has separate eligibility requirements, including a restriction related to full-time education, so do not assume a full-time undergraduate student qualifies.

A data journalist benefits more from demonstrable reporting and analysis than from accumulating certificates. Prioritise spreadsheet analysis, visualisation, statistics, verification and, later, SQL or Python.

Career progression

blocks.label: Year 1–2
blocks.text: Student Reporter / Fact-Checking Intern

blocks.label: Year 3–5
blocks.text: Junior Data Journalist / Researcher

blocks.label: Year 5–9
blocks.text: Data Journalist / Investigative Reporter

blocks.label: Year 9–14
blocks.text: Senior Data Journalist / Investigations Editor

blocks.label: Year 14+
blocks.text: Data Editor / Investigations Director / Independent Journalist
These are illustrative milestones, not fixed promotion timelines. Some journalists specialise deeply in analysis, while others move toward editorial management or independent investigations.
PhD routes
A PhD is optional for newsroom work but may suit someone who wants to research journalism, teach or develop new methods.

blocks.label: Journalism studies
blocks.text: News verification, investigative practices and data journalism.

blocks.label: Media and communication
blocks.text: Digital news, audience behaviour and platform effects.

blocks.label: Computational social science
blocks.text: Data-driven investigation of social and political trends, subject to quantitative prerequisites.

blocks.label: Public policy
blocks.text: Government accountability, public services and evidence-based policy reporting.

blocks.label: Information science
blocks.text: Data access, digital records, information integrity and archival research.
Check the institution's accepted qualifications, entrance requirements, supervisor availability and funding before applying.

2040–2046: remain relevant. Develop into a journalist who can both investigate a difficult question and explain the evidence clearly. Build expertise in reproducible analysis, source protection, statistical uncertainty, data privacy and responsible AI use. The strongest long-term advantage is the ability to ask good questions, verify claims independently and make complex evidence understandable to the public.
